title: Complexity separations for optimal matchgate-Clifford synthesis
authors: Berta Casas, Diego García-Martín, Yuxuan Zhang
abstract: Clifford and matchgate circuits are canonical families of classically simulable quantum circuits. Their intersection, the matchgate-Clifford group, plays an important role in randomized fermionic protocols and in matchgate synthesis. Its adjoint action is isomorphic to the group of unit-determinant signed permutations of $2n$ Majorana modes, and we study optimal exact synthesis in this group. That is, given a target unitary and a gate set, output an $n$-qubit circuit implementing the target using the fewest operations. We show that the complexity of this problem strongly depends on the gate set. In particular, we study gate sets consisting of Majorana braids with different connectivity graphs. For path and complete graphs, we prove that the problem is classically solvable in $\mathcal{O}\left(n^2\right)$ time, and we provide explicit gate-optimal compilers. In addition, we prove that when the connectivity graph is a tree, the decision version of the optimal synthesis problem becomes NP-complete. Finally, we benchmark our optimal compiler on chains of up to $n=80$ qubits against those of \texttt{Qiskit} and \texttt{Tket}, obtaining circuits with constant factor improvements $\times2.57$ and $\times2.28$ in the total number of gates, respectively.
summary: This paper analyzes the complexity of synthesizing target unitaries within the matchgate-Clifford group, which governs certain fermionic quantum protocols. It proves that while synthesis is efficiently solvable for simple graph structures like paths, the problem becomes NP-complete for general tree topologies. The work provides both theoretical complexity bounds and practical, high-performance compilers.
main_problem: The paper addresses the optimal unitary synthesis problem: finding the minimum number of gates required to implement a target unitary within the matchgate-Clifford group.
main_result: The optimal synthesis problem is efficiently solvable in polynomial time ($O(n^2)$) for path and complete connectivity graphs, but it is proven to be NP-complete for tree connectivity graphs.
method: The authors use algebraic methods involving potential functions ($\Phi(w)$) derived from the group structure of signed permutations, comparing the required gate count to established lower bounds.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum circuits restricted to the matchgate-Clifford group, whose structure is isomorphic to the group of unit-determinant signed permutations of $2n$ Majorana modes.
key_observables: Optimal gate count ($\ell_G(w)$), potential function ($\Phi(w)$), and the underlying signed permutation matrix ($w$).
important_parameters: The connectivity graph structure (Path, Complete, Tree) dictates the computational complexity of the synthesis problem.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on restricting the synthesis problem to specific graph topologies (path, complete, tree) to determine tractability.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of the proposed optimal compiler against Qiskit and Tket, showing constant factor improvements for chain simulations up to $n=80$ qubits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the problem formulation, deriving potential functions for specific graphs (path, complete), proving efficient solvability for these cases, and finally proving NP-completeness for the general tree case via reduction from token swapping.
why_interesting: The results provide concrete complexity boundaries for simulating fermionic quantum circuits, which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum simulation algorithms.

Randomly generated Clifford-matchgate circuits are compiled using different strategies: our optimal compiler, a Givens elimination strategy, sort then fix, pyket and Qiskit.
